headline: Stocks slip as Fed signals sustained rate hikes ahead
deck: Markets retreated modestly today as geopolitical tensions and monetary policy expectations weighed on investor sentiment.
body:
Equities finished in the red across all three major indices, with the growth-heavy Nasdaq leading declines at -0.80% while the Dow held up relatively better at -0.25%. The S&P 500 fell 0.45% to close at 760.88, reflecting a risk-off tone as investors digested fresh economic signals. Treasury yields ticked up slightly to 4.96%, consistent with a market bracing for continued Federal Reserve rate increases rather than near-term relief.

The CNBC survey confirming at least two Fed hikes over the next year appears to have reset expectations for monetary policy, suggesting any near-term rate cut hopes are premature. This backdrop makes growth stocks particularly vulnerable, explaining why the Nasdaq underperformed, and keeps bond yields anchored at elevated levels. The persistent inflation concerns implied by these rate expectations likely contributed to the broad-based selling pressure today.

Geopolitical developments added a secondary layer of uncertainty, with Middle East tensions affecting energy infrastructure and cloud services. AWS's outage in Bahrain following war damage and reports of intensifying attacks in the Hormuz region created supply-chain concerns, though some analysts note potential long-term commodity support if conflicts persist. These headline risks, combined with the Fed's hawkish messaging, created enough caution to keep risk appetite subdued through the session.
